title: FrogPop has a new trailer. Here's one of the smaller AI-assisted fixes behind the game
author: PerspectivePersonal
selftext:
I've been working on FrogPop, a Unity arcade roguelite about a frog popping bubbles. I shared the demo here last month. This is the new trailer for the full game.

One recent fix is a good example of how I'm using coding assistants now. The crab boss has a sweeping attack that still used two colored blocks as placeholders. I asked Codex to replace the effect, then asked for the danger zone to match the stork and snake bosses already in the game.

The effect now uses translucent bubble rings and foam. The warning uses the same red fill and border style as the other bosses. The attack timing, warning area and hitbox stayed the same.

That gave the task a clear limit: change how the attack looks while keeping its behavior. The checks covered the normal sweep, the return sweep, pausing and cleaning up the effect after the attack. I also reviewed it against the actual level background. This fix came after the trailer was recorded.

Across the project, I've used Claude and Codex for code and debugging, and PixelLab for some visual assets that I edited and integrated. There's no AI generation during play.

Free browser demo, first ten waves: [https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo](https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo)

Full game on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/)

The trailer includes later waves and bosses that aren't in the public demo.
